tagline: Home of the world's first Pilsner, with a walkable old town and UNESCO-listed underground tunnels.

taxi.fareNote: Use official taxi stands or apps (Bolt, Liftago); street-hailed cabs sometimes overcharge tourists.

emergency.note: General EU emergency number 112 also works and often has English-speaking operators.

hood_desc: The compact historic core centered on Republic Square, packed with Gothic and Renaissance facades, the cathedral, and the entrance to the underground tunnel network. Most sights, restaurants, and hotels are within a short walk here.
Home to the Pilsner Urquell brewery complex and its popular tours and beer spa; a mix of industrial heritage sites and casual pubs just east of the Old Town.
A green, residential district north of downtown built around the Bolevec fishponds, popular for walking, swimming, and cycling away from the tourist crowds.
A quiet southwestern district known for the city zoo and botanical garden, plus leafy suburban streets and family housing.
A mixed residential-commercial district just southeast of downtown with local shops, the historic Great Synagogue, and everyday Czech neighborhood life.

transit.pay: Contactless card tap, PMDP mobile app, or paper tickets from machines/kiosks
transit.note: Dense tram and trolleybus network (PMDP) covers the whole city; the Old Town itself is easily walkable.

train: Direct trains to Prague (~1.5hr) and Munich via České dráhy
bus: FlixBus and RegioJet coaches to Prague and other cities

tip.r: Round up or add 5-10% at sit-down restaurants; not expected for taxis, cafes, or takeaway.

tagline: Ancient West Bank city built around the revered Cave of the Patriarchs and a centuries-old stone souq.

taxi.fareNote: Shared 'service' taxis run fixed routes for a set per-person fare; private taxis should have the price agreed before departure.

emergency.note: Numbers reach Palestinian Civil Police and the Palestine Red Crescent Society. Hebron is administratively split into H1 (Palestinian Authority control) and H2 (Israeli military control) under the 1997 Hebron Protocol; movement through the Old City/H2 involves Israeli military checkpoints, and visitors should check current conditions before traveling, especially around the Old City and Ibrahimi Mosque area.

hood_landmark.Old City: Cave of the Patriarchs / Ibrahimi Mosque

hood_desc: The historic walled core containing the Ibrahimi Mosque/Cave of the Patriarchs, the centuries-old covered souq, and Mamluk-era stone architecture; part of this district (H2) is under Israeli military control with checkpoints and some closed streets.
A busy commercial spine south of the Old City with everyday shops, cafes, and street vendors popular with local Hebronites.
Home to Hebron's traditional glassblowing and ceramics workshops, a craft the city has practiced for centuries; visitors can watch artisans at work and buy directly from factory shops.
A residential and educational district anchored by Hebron University, with a younger, more modern feel than the Old City.
A dense commercial district around Bab al-Zawiya, one of the city's main market and transit hubs, with produce stalls, textiles, and shared-taxi stands.

transit.pay: Cash (shekels) paid directly to the driver
transit.map: No official transit map; ask your hotel or locals for current shared-taxi routes
transit.note: No formal public transit system or map; shared 'service' taxis and minibuses connect Hebron to Bethlehem, Ramallah, and other West Bank towns. Access to and movement within the Old City/H2 area can be affected by Israeli military checkpoints.

bus: Shared 'service' taxis and buses connect to Bethlehem and onward to Jerusalem/Ramallah checkpoints

tip.r: Tipping is uncommon; small gratuities are appreciated at restaurants but not required.

tagline: Storied university city of grand colleges, riverside punting, and quiet cloistered courtyards.

taxi.fareNote: Traditional black cabs are metered and can be hailed on the street; minicabs should be pre-booked by phone or app.

emergency.note: 999 for emergencies; 101 for non-emergency police; 112 also reaches emergency services.

hood_desc: The historic university core packed with ancient colleges, King's College Chapel, the Fitzwilliam Museum, and the main shopping streets; almost everything a visitor wants is within walking distance.
A lively, multicultural strip of independent cafes, ethnic restaurants, and vintage shops just east of the centre, favoured by students and locals over tourists.
The scenic stretch of green lawns and gardens along the River Cam behind the historic colleges, best known for punting and classic photo views of the bridges and chapels.
A residential riverside district north of the centre with parks, meadows, and a relaxed, family-friendly feel along the Cam.
A leafy, affluent residential area southwest of the centre near the university's science and arts faculties, with the Newnham College grounds and quiet mill pool.

transit.pay: Contactless card or phone tap, or Stagecoach smart ticketing app
transit.note: The city centre is compact and best explored on foot or by bike; Cambridge has one of the UK's highest cycling rates.

train: Direct trains to London King's Cross/Liverpool Street (~50 min)
bus: National Express coaches to London and major airports

tip.r: A 10-12.5% service charge is often added automatically at restaurants; round up for taxis and cafes if service was good.

tagline: Colonial highland city amid pine forests and Maya villages

taxi.fareNote: Unmetered taxis charge fixed in-town fares (roughly $30-50 MXN); agree on the price before getting in

emergency.note: 911 is Mexico's national emergency number; the historic center has good response, outlying villages less so

hood_desc: The heart of San Cristóbal, centered on the leafy Plaza de la Paz and its 16th-century cathedral. Cobblestone streets are lined with colonial buildings now housing cafes, galleries, and artisan shops. Most major sights, including the Santo Domingo church and the Na Bolom cultural center, are within walking distance.

A pedestrian-only street running east from the main plaza, packed with restaurants, bars, and live-music venues. It's the liveliest strip after dark, popular with backpackers passing through the Chiapas circuit. By day it doubles as a shopping street for amber jewelry and textiles.

A hillside neighborhood east of downtown, capped by the Templo de Guadalupe and its long staircase with panoramic valley views. Quieter and more residential than the center, with a small daily market at the foot of the steps. A good sunset spot away from the crowds.

Home to many of the city's textile and amber workshops, where Maya artisans sell handwoven huipiles and silver jewelry. The streets are narrower and more local than the tourist core. Good for browsing craft markets at a slower pace.

A traditional, working-class barrio on the northern edge of downtown, centered on its own small colonial chapel. Far fewer tourists venture here, giving a glimpse of everyday local life. Quiet in the evenings with simple family-run comedores.
lodging: Hotel Parador San Juan de Dios

transit.map: no formal transit map; informal combi routes
transit.note: The historic center is entirely walkable; colectivos and taxis connect outer neighborhoods and nearby villages like San Juan Chamula

air: Ángel Albino Corzo International Airport, Tuxtla Gutiérrez (TGZ)
bus: OCC/ADO buses to Tuxtla Gutiérrez, Palenque, Oaxaca, and Mexico City

tip.r: Tipping 10-15% at restaurants is standard; round up for taxis; tip guides on tours

tagline: Laid-back trekking base at the foot of Mount Kilimanjaro

taxi.fareNote: Taxis are unmetered; negotiate the fare before departure, typically TSh 3,000-8,000 within town

emergency.note: 112 is Tanzania's national emergency number; serious medical cases are referred to Kilimanjaro Christian Medical Centre (KCMC) or Arusha

hood_desc: The commercial core of Moshi, anchored by the landmark clock tower roundabout and the bustling central market. Tour operators, banks, and shops line the grid of streets, with Kilimanjaro often visible on clear mornings. Most climbers organize trek logistics here.

A cluster of guesthouses, bars, and trekking outfitters just west of the center, popular with backpackers and climbing groups before and after a Kilimanjaro summit. Livelier after dark than the rest of Moshi, with a handful of expat-friendly bars. Convenient walking distance to the main market.

A quieter, tree-lined residential area dating to the colonial railway era, with older bungalow-style houses. It's mostly local families rather than tourists. A calm base if you want distance from the tourist bustle.

A local residential neighborhood on Moshi's outskirts, close to the smaller Kiboriloni market. Few tourists stay here, but it offers an authentic look at daily Chagga town life. Simple guesthouses and food stalls serve the area.

The coffee-growing highlands above Moshi on the lower slopes of Kilimanjaro, dotted with Chagga homesteads and banana groves. Popular for half-day coffee tours and waterfall hikes. Noticeably cooler and greener than the town below.

transit.map: no formal map; informal routes, ask locals
transit.note: Dala-dalas connect Moshi to surrounding villages; walking and taxis or boda-bodas cover the town center

bus: Buses to Arusha, Dar es Salaam, and Nairobi

tip.r: 10% tip at restaurants when service isn't included; tip trekking guides and porters generously (roughly $15-20/day for guides, $8-10/day for porters)

tagline: Sacred Yoruba city famed for its UNESCO grove and river festival

taxi.fareNote: Shared taxis and keke napep (auto-rickshaws) are common; negotiate fares before boarding since meters aren't used

emergency.note: 112 is Nigeria's national emergency number; response can be slow, so private hospitals are recommended for serious issues

hood_desc: Osogbo's central market and traditional seat of power, next to the Ataoja of Osogbo's palace. Stalls sell everything from Yoruba textiles to fresh produce in a dense, noisy grid of lanes. It's the commercial and civic heart of the city.

The forested riverside district holding the UNESCO-listed Osun-Osogbo Sacred Grove, dotted with shrines and sculptures dedicated to the river goddess Osun. It becomes the epicenter of the Osun-Osogbo Festival every August, drawing worshippers and visitors from across Nigeria and the diaspora. Otherwise it's a peaceful, shaded walk along the river.

An older quarter along the Osun River, one of the original settlement areas of the city. Traditional compound houses and small shrines reflect Osogbo's deep Yoruba religious roots. Life moves slowly here compared to the busier market districts.

A busy commercial strip lined with shops, tailors, and roadside vendors, popular for everyday shopping and street food. It sits along one of Osogbo's main transport corridors. Good for keke napep connections across town.

A largely residential neighborhood on higher ground overlooking the city center. It's a quiet area of family compounds with little tourist infrastructure. Mostly relevant to visitors staying with local hosts or attending events nearby.

transit.map: no formal map; informal shared routes
transit.note: Keke napep tricycles and shared taxis are the main way to get around; agree on the fare before boarding

train: Nigerian Railway Lagos-Kano (western line) stops in Osogbo
bus: ABC Transport and God is Good Motors buses to Lagos, Ibadan, and Abuja

tip.r: Tipping isn't deeply ingrained locally, but rounding up or 10% in hotels and restaurants catering to visitors is appreciated

tagline: A sun-warmed Hungarian city of Ottoman-era mosques, Zsolnay ceramics, and Roman-era tombs beneath its streets

taxi.fareNote: Official taxis have yellow plates and roof signs; confirm the meter is running or agree a fare in advance, especially from the train station

emergency.note: 112 is the EU-wide emergency number; Hungary's older direct lines (107 police, 104 ambulance, 105 fire) also still work

hood_landmark.Belváros: Pécs Cathedral & Mosque of Pasha Qasim

hood_desc: Pécs' walkable historic core, centered on Széchenyi Square and the former Ottoman-era Pasha Qasim Mosque. Cobbled lanes lead to Pécs Cathedral, the Zsolnay Fountain, and the city's best cafés and shops.

The beautifully restored 19th-century Zsolnay porcelain factory grounds, now a cultural quarter of museums, galleries, and design shops. It's the best place to see the manufacturer's famous iridescent eosin glaze up close.

A leafy hillside above downtown with the ruins of a 16th-century Ottoman garden pavilion and sweeping views over Pécs' rooftops. Quiet trails and a small chapel make it a favorite for an evening walk.
A mostly residential district of socialist-era apartment blocks built for uranium-mining families in the 1950s-60s. It offers a glimpse of everyday, non-touristy Pécs with local markets and parks.
A newer suburban district on the city's edge with shopping centers and family housing. Handy for practical errands but with little of historic interest.

transit.hours: Buses run roughly 5am-11pm, reduced frequency on weekends
transit.pay: Single tickets bought on board or from machines; multi-day passes available
transit.note: The historic center is compact and best explored on foot; buses mainly serve outlying districts

air: Budapest Ferenc Liszt International Airport (BUD) - main gateway, ~200km away
Pécs-Pogány Airport (PEV) - tiny local airport with very limited seasonal flights
train: Direct trains to/from Budapest, roughly 2.5-3 hours
bus: Volánbusz coaches connect Pécs with Budapest and regional towns

tip.r: Rounding up or leaving about 10% in restaurants is customary when service is good; not expected for taxis or small purchases

tagline: Home to the world's largest carved stone Buddha, watching over three rivers at the edge of the Sichuan Basin

taxi.fareNote: Official taxis are metered but drivers rarely speak English; having your destination written in Chinese characters or using the DiDi app is essential

emergency.note: 110 for police, 120 for medical emergencies, 119 for fire - standard nationwide numbers; English-speaking operators are not guaranteed

hood_desc: The riverside cliffs holding the 71-meter Leshan Giant Buddha, carved directly into the rock during the Tang dynasty. The surrounding park includes viewing platforms, Lingyun Temple, and steep stairways carved alongside the statue.
A wooded hill across the river from the Buddha, home to the ancient Wuyou Temple and its 1,000 carved arhat statues. Reached by bridge or boat, it's far less crowded than the main Buddha site.

Leshan's historic riverside streets, famous across Sichuan for snack stalls selling specialties like tofu pudding (dou fu nao) and grilled skewers. It's the best place to sample the city's celebrated street food scene at night.

The main riverside promenade in central Leshan, with parks, night markets, and views over the confluence of the Min, Dadu, and Qingyi rivers where the Buddha overlooks the water. Restaurants and hotels cluster along this strip.

The base town for Mount Emei, one of China's four sacred Buddhist mountains and a UNESCO World Heritage Site paired with the Giant Buddha. Cable cars and trails climb to temples and the Golden Summit, often above the clouds.

transit.pay: Cash, transit card, or WeChat/Alipay QR scan
transit.note: No metro; most visitors reach the Buddha via scenic-area shuttle bus or a sightseeing boat on the river

air: Chengdu Shuangliu International Airport (CTU) - main gateway, ~120km
Chengdu Tianfu International Airport (TFU) - newer hub, ~160km
train: Chengdu-Emeishan-Leshan high-speed rail, about 1 hour from Chengdu East
bus: Long-distance coaches from Chengdu Xinnanmen bus station, about 2 hours
ferry: Sightseeing boats on the Min River offer views of the Giant Buddha from the water

car.idp: Not recognized - China does not honor the IDP; self-drive is impractical for tourists, hire a licensed local driver instead

tip.r: Tipping is not part of local culture and can seem confusing to service staff; not expected in restaurants, taxis, or hotels

tagline: A medieval walled city of Gothic spires, Viking history, and the crooked shop-lined lanes of The Shambles

taxi.fareNote: Licensed hackney carriages (often white in York) can be hailed on the street or found at ranks; private hire cars must be pre-booked by phone or app

emergency.note: 999 for emergencies (112 also works); 101 for non-emergency police, 111 for non-emergency NHS medical advice

hood_desc: The walled heart of York, packed inside the medieval city walls around York Minster and the crooked, timber-framed Shambles. It's the most touristed part of the city, dense with shops, museums, and historic pubs.
A steep street of Georgian townhouses leading up from Micklegate Bar, long known as York's main nightlife strip of bars and clubs. By day it's quieter, lined with independent shops and cafés.
A relaxed residential street just outside the walls, nicknamed 'Bishy Road,' known for its independent cafés, delis, and boutiques. It has a villagey feel popular with locals rather than tourists.

A cluster of narrow streets east of the center that has become York's creative quarter, full of craft-beer pubs, vintage shops, and the medieval Merchant Adventurers' Hall. It's one of the liveliest areas after dark without the Micklegate crowds.

A leafy residential district just north of the walls along the River Ouse, mixing Victorian terraces with green space at Clifton Green. It's a peaceful, mostly local area a short walk from the center.

transit.hours: Buses run approximately 6am-11:30pm, frequent on main routes
transit.pay: Contactless card, mobile app, or cash on board
transit.note: The walled city center is fully walkable; Park & Ride buses are useful for reaching in from car parks on the outskirts

train: York station is a major stop on the East Coast Main Line: London ~2 hours, Edinburgh ~2h15m, Leeds ~25 min
bus: National Express coaches serve York from major UK cities

car.idp: Not required for short visits - most foreign licenses valid up to 12 months

tip.r: A 10-12.5% service charge is often added automatically at restaurants; if not, tipping around 10% is customary. Not expected in pubs or taxis, though rounding up is appreciated
